MathTex and Tex

Source: R/tex.R
tex.Rd

LaTeX rendered to vectorized mobjects. MathTex() typesets math (in an align* environment), Tex() typesets text mode LaTeX. Each string argument becomes one submobject, so MathTex("a^2", "+", "b^2")[3] is the b^2 part. Double braces {{ ... }} also split parts. tex_to_color_map colors matching parts.

Usage

SingleStringMathTex(
  tex_string,
  stroke_width = 0,
  should_center = TRUE,
  height = NULL,
  organize_left_to_right = FALSE,
  tex_environment = "align*",
  tex_template = NULL,
  font_size = DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
  color = NULL,
  ...
)

MathTex(
  ...,
  arg_separator = " ",
  substrings_to_isolate = NULL,
  tex_to_color_map = NULL,
  tex_environment = "align*",
  tex_template = NULL
)

Tex(..., arg_separator = "", tex_environment = "center")

Arguments

tex_string

A single LaTeX string.

stroke_width

Stroke width.

should_center

Center at the origin.

height

Optional height.

organize_left_to_right

Sort glyphs by x.

tex_environment

LaTeX environment.

tex_template

A TexTemplate().

font_size

Font size (48 by default).

color

Color.

...

Strings (or values coerced to strings), then named arguments.

arg_separator

Separator between the strings.

substrings_to_isolate

Substrings to make addressable parts.

tex_to_color_map

Named list mapping substrings to colors.

Value

A mobject: an R6 object of the class named by the function called. The objects whose names end in Class are the R6 class generators that these functions call.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs LaTeX and dvisvgm.
MathTex("e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0")
Tex("Hello \\LaTeX", color = BLUE)
} # }
